assumptions: The DSL models the discrete Stateflow supervisor only. Wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, PID computation, and continuous wheel-slip plant dynamics are treated as external to this FSM; their supervisor-facing result is represented by the input variable `slp`.
No explicit initial state was specified beyond the listed state order, so the synthesized root initializes to the first listed state, `increase`.

transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands: `increase -> hold` when `slp <= 0.01`

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: the synthesized initial transition should enter increase and apply increase outputs k1=1, k2=0, n=0.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: increase must transition to hold when slp is exactly 0.01 and hold must neutralize outputs.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_slp_0_01

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: increase must not transition to hold when slp is above 0.01.
scenario_results.name: increase_stays_above_slp_0_01

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary no-fire probe: hold must not transition to increase when slp is exactly 0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start threshold probe: hold must transition to increase when slp is greater than 0.01 and increase must command inlet pressure increase.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_slp_0_01

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary no-fire probe: hold must not transition to decrease when slp is exactly -0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start threshold probe: hold must transition to decrease when slp is less than -0.01, then remain in decrease while slp stays below -0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: decrease must transition to hold when slp is exactly -0.01 and hold must neutralize valve and pump outputs.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary

evidence: NL requires states increase, hold, decrease with outputs increase: k1=1,k2=0,n=0; hold: k1=0,k2=0,n=0; decrease: k1=0,k2=1,n=500.
DSL implements state increase/hold/decrease with matching during assignments.
NL requires transitions increase->hold slp<=0.01, hold->increase slp>0.01, hold->decrease slp<-0.01, decrease->hold slp>=-0.01.
DSL implements the same four guarded transitions.
findings.summary: The DSL is faithful to the NL-described discrete three-state hydraulic supervisor: states, constant valve/pump outputs, and four threshold guards match the specification.

evidence: NL: wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL declares only slp, k1, k2, and n; no wheel speed, vehicle speed, PID state, PID gains, integrator, derivative term, or plant dynamics are modeled.
GroundingMap.source_summary.assumptions states that wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, PID computation, and continuous dynamics are external to this FSM and represented by slp.
findings.summary: The PID controller, wheel-speed/vehicle-speed slip computation, and continuous plant dynamics mentioned in the NL are abstracted away into the external variable slp. This is acceptable only if the intended scope is the discrete Stateflow supervisor.

evidence: Current DSL models only threshold-driven transitions over slp.
five_component_summary is empty, so there is no independent evidence of FE/NGF/REC/GAS/SCB/AAT/BVS/DMR-style coverage for the omitted continuous/PID portions.
Simulation scenarios validate threshold behavior but not PID-to-supervisor coupling.
findings.summary: The model is a good abstraction of the discrete supervisor but not of the full paper-level ABS regulator with coupled PID/slip dynamics.

evidence: DSL: decrease -> hold : if [slp >= -0.01]
sim_summary scenario decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary passed with state hold and outputs k1=0,k2=0,n=0 at slp=-0.01.
findings.summary: No unsafe recovery behavior is evident within the modeled supervisor; decrease recovers to hold at slp >= -0.01 as required.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.nl_external_input_vars includes slp.
Diagnostics include W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for slp, consistent with slp being an external supervisor input.
Diagnostics include W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, and likely n; these variables are pure commanded outputs rather than guard-driving internal variables.
findings.summary: External input and pure outputs are not explicitly separated in the DSL declarations, which causes advisory diagnostics but does not contradict the NL.

evidence: Diagnostics include W_DURING_CONST_ASSIGN for k1, k2, and n in all three states.

findings.summary: No unjustified warning-driven repair is present. The constant during assignments flagged by diagnostics are directly required by the NL state output mapping.
